chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Zurara, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the one performing Itikaaf who sleeps with his wife. He (peace be upon him) said: 'When he does, so upon him would be what is upon the one who does Zihaar'.

key_terms.الْمُظَاهِرِ: The one who performs Zihaar (a specific form of divorce/oath)
key_terms.مَا عَلَى: What is upon / the penalty of
key_terms.يُجَامِعُ: He has sexual intercourse / sleeps with

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for a person performing Itikaaf who has sexual intercourse with their spouse?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi, transmitted through the chain of Zurarah to Imam al-Baqir, establishes that sexual intercourse during Itikaaf incurs the same expiation (kaffarah) as Zihaar, a ruling derived from the Quranic verse in Surah al-Mujadila. This equivalence highlights the severity of breaking the sanctity of the mosque retreat, treating it with the same legal weight as the major divorce form prevalent in pre-Islamic Arabia. The ruling underscores the continuity of Shia jurisprudence in applying Quranic penalties to specific ritual violations.
